question: Someone is asking for my OTP. Should I share it?
answer: Never share your One-Time Password (OTP) with anyone under any circumstances. SafePay, banks, government officials, and police will NEVER ask for your OTP.
simple_answer: NO! Never tell your OTP code to anyone. Not to anyone calling you, not to friends, not even to bank staff. Giving your OTP allows strangers to steal your money.
steps: Do not reply to the message
safety_warning: DANGER: Anyone asking for your OTP is trying to take money from your bank account.

question: Someone asked me for my UPI PIN. What should I do?
answer: Your UPI PIN is your private digital signature. Never type your PIN on anyone else's phone, on websites, or share it in calls, messages, or chat.
simple_answer: DO NOT SHARE IT. Your PIN is like the key to your house locker. SafePay will never ask for your PIN. Only type your PIN when you are paying.
steps: Never write or tell your PIN to anyone
Do not enter it in any chat window
If you suspect someone saw it, change it immediately in bank settings
safety_warning: CRITICAL: Never share your UPI PIN with anyone, including customer support.

question: I got a message saying I won a prize or lottery of ₹50,000, but I must pay ₹500 fee first. Is it real?
answer: This is an advance-fee fraud scam. Genuine lotteries or cashbacks never demand payment of processing fees, taxes, or registration charges upfront.
simple_answer: This is a scam. You have not won any lottery. Real prizes never ask you to pay money first to collect your prize. Do not send any money.
steps: Do not send the ₹500 or any amount
Report the message in our Safety Center
safety_warning: WARNING: Any message asking for money to release a prize is a scam.

question: A message says my bank account or SIM card will be blocked unless I update KYC by clicking a link.
answer: Banks never send APK files, third-party download links, or threaten immediate account suspension via personal SMS. This is a KYC phishing attempt.
simple_answer: Do not click that link! Banks will never block your account through a simple message or ask you to update KYC on an unknown link. It is a fraud attempt.
steps: Do not click any link in the SMS
Do not call the phone number in the message
Visit your real bank branch if you have any questions
safety_warning: Do not install apps or click links sent in SMS claiming to update KYC.

question: I think I was scammed or sent money to a fraudster. What should I do right now?
answer: Act immediately: Dial the national cyber fraud helpline 1930 within the golden hour, report the transaction to your bank to freeze the recipient account, and report it on cybercrime.gov.in.
simple_answer: Call 1930 immediately! That is the official police cyber helpline. Call your bank right away and tell them you were tricked so they can try to stop the money.
steps: Call your bank customer care immediately
Take screenshots of the payment and messages
safety_warning: Call 1930 immediately to freeze funds before the scammer withdraws them.
